items.title: Joseph Thomas Interview, 1960-09-29
items.q: when I joined the band, he had a smaller band... But, uh, the time I'm talking about, he, oh, he had a, oh, big, uh, brass band

ctx.x: Yes. Uh, this other clarinet. Now, let me see if that's the one I bought by Peterson or the one I got from, uh, well, I guess it matters. It don't matter which place I got it from. It's Noble. Noble. Noble, yes. Oh, Noble. Yeah. Never heard of that. That's a, that's a BEM you're speaking about. It's a BEM, yes. Um, BEMs and Noble and all. The other one I can't remember now, but I might remember the name before we finish. Well, anyhow. Uh, so let me, right now I have three clarinets. What are you still doing?…
Uh, you were mentioning about, uh, Papa Salastain, uh, knocking out with the, uh, two-by-four. Did he do that in later years when you joined the band?

No, no, no, he didn't. You just, uh, when I joined the band, he had a smaller band than, uh, uh, seven or eight pieces of the moors. Perhaps ten when we had to play at the hotels that called for ten pieces or some of these halls, you know, called for ten pieces. But, uh, the time I'm talking about, he, oh, he had a, oh, big, uh, brass band, I think it was, like, uh, about twenty pieces.
